title: Sep 22 Results + Sep 23 Preview: 60% Ain't Sexy, But I'll Take the Money
summary: Sep 22 went 9-6 with some ugly losses. Tomorrow? Tigers or bust with Valdez dealing.

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: 60% Is Mediocre

Look, I'm not here to sugarcoat this. Going 9-6 on September 22nd is the definition of 'meh.' Sure, we're above .500, and yeah, that technically means profit if you're betting units correctly. But let's call it what it is—we left money on the table with some absolutely boneheaded losses that should've never happened.

## The Damage Report

The Rays double-header was peak chaos—we split it like a confused bettor at a roulette table. Lost the first, won the second. The Tigers choked against the Nationals when we gave them 62% odds. The Cubs at 61% confidence? Embarrassing miss. And don't even get me started on the Rangers pick at basically a coin flip. That was desperation, and we paid for it.

content.value:
## What Went Right (Give Credit Where It's Due)

The Pirates at 62%? Money. Guardians and Sox both came through in tight spots. When we hit on the mid-50% picks, those are actually the most satisfying because they're basically telling Vegas to shut up. The second Rays game saved us from a truly pathetic doubleheader performance.

## Tomorrow's Revenge Tour: Sep 23

Here's where it gets spicy. We're rolling with the **Detroit Tigers** against the Nationals again. Yeah, I know—they just burned us yesterday at 62%. But here's the thing: Framber Valdez is on the mound for Detroit, and Richard Lovelady is throwing for Washington. This isn't rocket science, people.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 23 Top Pick
content.sub: 61% win probability vs Nationals | Valdez vs Lovelady is a mismatch

content.value:
## Why Tigers Again? Am I Insane?

Maybe. But hear me out. Framber Valdez has been dealing, and Lovelady—bless his heart with that name—isn't exactly striking fear into anyone's heart. The model says 61%, and after yesterday's debacle, Detroit owes us. This is a classic bounce-back spot.

The Nationals got lucky yesterday. Lightning doesn't strike twice. And if it does? Well, then I'll come back here tomorrow and roast myself. But I'm confident, borderline arrogant even, that Detroit takes this one.

**The hot take:** If you're not hammering Tigers tomorrow, you're betting scared. And scared money don't make money.

## Final Word

Sep 22 was fine. Not great, not terrible. We made money, stayed disciplined (mostly), and lived to bet another day. Tomorrow's a new slate, and I'm doubling down on Detroit because sometimes you gotta trust the process even when it punches you in the gut.

See you on the other side. Let's get this money.

— Rico
